intro: Version ordering is hierarchical. A larger major version wins even if every later component is smaller, and numeric comparison avoids treating 10 as less than 2.
task: Parse and compare strict numeric major.minor.patch versions without prerelease syntax.
requirements: Each trimmed version is three ASCII digit components separated by dots. Each component is 0..1e9; leading zeros are allowed. Return -1, 0, or 1 by numeric lexicographic comparison. Reject prerelease/build suffixes and other component counts.

Text inputs contain valid Unicode scalar characters and at most 10000 characters. Integer inputs must be Python ints, excluding bool, within the task-specific bounds or -1e9..1e9 when no narrower bounds are stated.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Parse all three components as integers, then compare tuples.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Stop at the first unequal component; later components cannot override it.

explanation: Version ordering is hierarchical. A larger major version wins even if every later component is smaller, and numeric comparison avoids treating 10 as less than 2.
This exercise implements a restricted triple format, not the complete semantic-version specification. Rejecting unsupported suffixes keeps that distinction explicit.
